method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; NOTHING-kind where it does not answer); the one date in a small module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; one regulative rule (the s 28 prohibition on disclosing information obtained in administering the Act, SHANT) run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

seat: a person with a claim on the Motor Accidents (Compensation) Commission: usually the person injured in a motor accident, or a dependant after a death, claiming under the MAC scheme of the Motor Accidents (Compensation) Act 1979; also a former Territory Insurance Office customer whose policy or deposit stayed with the Commission (ntmaccc-claims.l4)

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text. A deliberately wrong assertion on the s 28 rule was run once in a scratch copy and showed as 'assertion failed'.

scope: The provisions of the Act a claimant meets. In: s 3 (MAC business, MAC scheme, Fund), s 5, s 7(a), s 8, s 9, s 11, s 12(3), s 15, s 16(2), (3), s 17(2), s 18, s 27, s 28, s 30, ss 31, 33, 34, s 43. Out: ss 1, 2, 4, 6, 10, 12(1), (2), 13, 14, 16(1), 17(1), 19-26, 29, 32, 36-42 (the Commission's constitution, management, finances and reporting; s 26 borrows Government Owned Corporations Act sections not deposited; s 39 rewrites references in other Acts). Reasons in NOTES.md.
